sec: Screening, early therapy, cirrhosis pathology and fibrosis staging

items.q: Which of the following conditions is NOT listed under routine screening for chronic hepatitis on this page?
opts: Autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson's disease, and Hemochromatosis
items.exp: Routine screening covers NASH, HBV/HCV, Autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson's disease, and Hemochromatosis. (Book p998)

items.q: Match each cause of chronic liver disease with the early intervention that yields very good therapeutic outcomes — 1) Hemochromatosis 2) Wilson's disease 3) NASH … A) Early penicillamine therapy B) Weight loss C) Early phlebotomy
items.exp: Treatment before/during progression yields good outcomes with early phlebotomy for hemochromatosis, early penicillamine for Wilson's, and weight loss for NASH. (Book p998)

items.q: What is the defining pathological definition of cirrhosis?
opts: Normal lobular architecture lost and replaced by nodules connected by fibrous septation
Centrilobular hemorrhagic necrosis without architectural remodeling
Microvesicular steatosis confined to zone 3 hepatocytes
Isolated granulomatous destruction of interlobular bile ducts
items.exp: Cirrhosis is defined as: 'Normal lobular architecture of liver lost and replaced by nodules connected by fibrous septation.' (Book p998)

items.q: Fill up: On gross surgical and post-mortem inspection, a cirrhotic liver characteristically presents with a ______ colour, irregular surface, and nodular texture.
items.exp: The specimen caption describes: 'Cirrhotic liver lives with tawny brown colour irregular surface and nodular texture'. (Book p998)

items.q: What microscopic feature distinguishes a cirrhotic liver from normal hepatic parenchyma?
opts: Disorganised architecture with regenerative nodules surrounded by fibrous septa
Preserved hexaconal lobules radiating from central veins
Pure portal triad inflammation without any stromal septa
Complete absence of biliary ductules and endothelial fenestrations
items.exp: Microscopy shows 'Disorganised architecture with regenerative nodule surrounded by fibrous septa'. (Book p998)

items.q: Match each stage of hepatic fibrosis with its histopathological definition — 1) Stage 1 2) Stage 2 3) Stage 3 4) Stage 4 … A) 2+ Bridging fibrosis extending to the next portal tract B) 3+ Nodules representing full-blown cirrhosis C) Mild periportal fibrosis D) 1+ Septation
items.exp: The staging runs: Stage 1 = mild periportal fibrosis, Stage 2 = 1+ septation, Stage 3 = 2+ bridging fibrosis extending to next portal tract, and Stage 4 = 3+ nodules (full-blown cirrhosis). (Book p998)

items.q: Fill up: In the staging of hepatic fibrosis, Stage 3 is characterised by ______ fibrosis extending across to the next portal tract.
items.exp: Stage 3 is defined as '2+ Bridging fibrosis : Fibrosis extending to next portal tract'. (Book p998)

items.q: Assess the two statements on hepatic fibrosis staging: I Stage 2 fibrosis is defined by 1+ septation without complete architectural nodularity. II Stage 4 represents full-blown cirrhosis characterized by regenerative nodules surrounded by fibrous septa.
items.exp: Both statements are true: Stage 2 has 1+ septation, and Stage 4 has 3+ nodules defining full-blown cirrhosis. (Book p998)

items.q: A liver biopsy specimen from a 49-year-old patient with chronic Hepatitis C demonstrates fibrous bands extending from one portal triad to an adjacent portal tract, but without complete regenerative nodule formation. What fibrosis stage is present?
items.exp: Fibrosis extending to the next portal tract without nodules is Stage 3 (2+ bridging fibrosis). (Book p998)

items.q: Which intervention is specifically noted on this page to achieve a good outcome when instituted early in NASH?
items.exp: Under treatment during progression, NASH is paired with 'weight loss -> Good outcome'. (Book p998)
